newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy falls sharply on Brazilian soy imports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy falls sharply on Brazilian soy imports.

text.p: CBOT soybeans and soymeal fell sharply in fast trading in response to confirmation that at least one major U.S. firm was importing soybeans from Brazil, floor traders said.
"The news is not surprising but is certainly negative for soybeans," said one floor trader.
Cargill, Inc, confirmed Wednesday that it was importing soybeans from Brazil to meet supply needs in the U.S.

"Cargill has contracted to import soybeans from Brazil for use in our procssing plants in the southeastern United States where the (soybean) shortage is particularly acute," the company said in a statement.
On Tuesday, U.S. poultry producer Tyson Foods Inc. said it would accept soymeal from suppliers who had crushed South American soybeans.
At 1051 CDT, CBOT soybeans were 21 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 21 at $8.39 per bushel. Soymeal futures were $7.60 to $0.20 per ton, with July down $7.40 at $275.40.
